name: Steve Novick

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Novick was elected District 3 city councilor in November 2024 and began his term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 3 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

bio.statement: Novick's voters' pamphlet statement lists work as a federal Justice Department lawyer suing polluters from 1987 to 1996.
bio.excerpt: Federal Justice Department lawyer, suing polluters, 1987-96;

bio.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement lists work at the Oregon Justice Department from 2018 to 2024 opposing federal environmental rollbacks.
bio.excerpt: Oregon Justice Department, fighting Trump environmental rollbacks, 2018-24.

bio.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement lists a BA from the University of Oregon (1981) and a JD from Harvard Law School (1984).
bio.excerpt: B.A., University of Oregon, 1981; J.D., Harvard Law School, 1984.

bio.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement lists prior service as Portland City Commissioner from 2013 to 2016.

positions.statement: Novick's voters' pamphlet statement says he has fought to cut what it calls bloated budgets.
positions.excerpt: Steve Novick has fought to cut the bloated budgets

positions.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement says he is pushing to shift 911 welfare-check calls from police to less expensive unarmed personnel.
positions.excerpt: Steve is pushing to shift 911 “welfare check” calls from police officers to less expensive unarmed personnel.

positions.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement says he voted against increasing the Arts Tax.
positions.excerpt: Steve voted against increasing the Arts Tax.

positions.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement says he wants to keep the Blazers while ensuring the city gets as much from the Moda Center as it puts in.
positions.excerpt: Steve wants to keep the Blazers, while making sure that we get as much money out of the Moda Center as we put in.

positions.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement says he pushed the Police Bureau to expand its use of Oregon's red flag law.
positions.excerpt: Steve successfully pushed the Police Bureau to dramatically expand its use of the “red flag law,”

positions.statement: Novick's pamphlet statement says he opposed proposed cuts to the city office that helps small businesses with graffiti and vandalism.
positions.excerpt: He fought some councilors’ proposed cuts to the city office that helps small businesses with graffiti and vandalism.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Novick lists making the parks system sustainable without another tax increase as a priority.
positions.excerpt: Making the parks system sustainable without asking voters for another tax increase.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Novick has spoken against using the Clean Energy Fund to renovate the Moda Center.
positions.excerpt: has spoken out against using the city’s Clean Energy Fund for renovating the Moda Center

gaps: City filing form (AUD-120) text contained no candidate fields

collection_log.result: nothing relevant (fetched; candidate not mentioned or nothing usable beyond other sources)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Incumbent per portland.gov/council. Date discrepancy: pamphlet lists commissioner service 2013-16; OPB says 2013 to 2017.
